answer: Verifiable-delay proofs resist sybils: each identity must publish a VDF output, a cipher producible only by running a fixed number of strictly SEQUENTIAL steps, unparallelizable by construction. One honest agent computes its single delay chain; an attacker wanting K live identities must run K separate chains, and no hardware collapses sequential time, so a velvet-fast farm cannot batch them. Minting clones grows like a vine only as fast as real wall-clock allows per key: total delay-work scales linearly in K with no parallel shortcut, pricing mass identities in time itself.
